To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) combination mAb treatment may be an effective therapeutic approach against smallpox disease and (2) combination mAb therapy may also be an effective therapeutic option against monkeypox disease.
combination mAb therapy provides significantly better protection against VACV infection than either single mAb or vaccinia immunoglobulin.
combination hmAb prophylactic therapy is effective at controlling small-pox disease in immunodeficient mice and rabbitpox disease in rabbits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing novel therapeutics against poxvirus disease.
the development of novel, fully human mAbs against smallpox, which are being evaluated as potential therapeutics to treat smallpox disease and prevent the spread of smallpox.

the combination hmAb therapy provides significant protection against smallpox and RPXV infections in both rabbits and immunocompromised SCID mice, and that the combination mAbs may be effective at treating smallpox in immunocompetence humans.
combination hmAbs provide significant protection against smallpox in both immunocompetent and immunodeficient animals.
fully human antibodies targeting both the MV and EV forms of VACV are effective at controlling lethal smallpox and rabbitpox infections in both immunodeficient and immunocompetent animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fully human mAbs against vaccinia H2 and B5 are highly protective against lethal poxviral infections in both rabbits and SCID mice.

the combination of two hmAbs targeting the mature virion and extracellular envelop forms of vaccinia virus, H3L and B5, can protect both rabbits and immunodeficient mice against lethal infections of vaccinia, monkeypox and rabbitpox viruses, and that this therapy is effective when given either pre- or post-exposure.
fully human mAbs against vaccinia H and B5, which are conserved poxvirus antigens, can protect rabbits and SCID mice against lethal poxviral infections.

combination hmAb prophylactic therapy is highly effective in both rabbits and mice.
fully human monoclonal antibodies against vaccinia virus can be effective in protecting rabbits and immunodeficient mice from lethal poxviral infections.
